title: IPL 2026 Playoff Race Heats Up as KKR Stun Gujarat in Eden Gardens Run-Fest
excerpt: Finn Allen's 93 off 35 balls powers Kolkata to 247, but six teams still fight for four spots with ten matches left
body:
Finn Allen announced himself in the most emphatic way possible on Friday evening. Walking out to bat at Eden Gardens with his team's season on the line, the New Zealander smashed 93 off just 35 deliveries — a brutal, boundary-laden assault that propelled Kolkata Knight Riders to 247 for 2, one of the highest totals in IPL history, and a 29-run victory over Gujarat Titans.

The win keeps KKR's playoff hopes flickering, but the broader story of IPL 2026's league stage is the fierce, unresolved battle for the final two playoff berths. With ten matches remaining and six teams still mathematically alive, the tournament's business end is delivering the kind of uncertainty that makes the IPL the world's most-watched cricket league — and a fortnightly obsession for millions of diaspora fans streaming from living rooms in New Jersey, London, and Toronto.

## The table as it stands

Royal Challengers Bengaluru sit atop the standings with 16 points from 12 matches, their net run rate of +1.053 providing a comfortable cushion. Gujarat Titans, despite Friday's stumble at Eden Gardens, are level on 16 points but with an inferior NRR. Both look near-certain to qualify. Sunrisers Hyderabad (14 points) hold third place with a game in hand over some rivals.

The real drama is below. Punjab Kings (13 points), Rajasthan Royals (12 from 11 matches), and Chennai Super Kings (12 from 12) are locked in a three-way fight for the fourth and final playoff spot. A single result over the next week could rearrange this cluster entirely. Delhi Capitals (10 points) are technically alive but need an improbable combination of results and NRR swings.

## Narine's milestone, Siraj's record

Friday's match at Eden Gardens was rich in milestones. Sunil Narine, who returned figures of 2 for 29 to strangle Gujarat's middle order, played his 200th match for KKR — the first overseas player to reach that landmark for a single IPL franchise. The Trinidadian all-rounder, who Ambati Rayudu this week described as "the best IPL player of all time," remains an irreplaceable figure in Kolkata's attack even in his 17th IPL season.

On the other side, Gujarat's Mohammed Siraj claimed his 200th T20 wicket during the match, a quiet milestone for a bowler whose career has been defined by perseverance through early-career ridicule and personal tragedy.

## Shubman Gill's consolation

Gujarat captain Shubman Gill, batting with characteristic elegance, scored 85 in a losing cause. Jos Buttler added 57. But chasing 248 was always going to be a tall order, and Gujarat's bowlers — Kagiso Rabada and Rashid Khan included — had no answer to Allen's onslaught in the powerplay.

https://www.instagram.com/p/shubmangill

Gill's form is not in question; his team's bowling depth is. Gujarat have now lost back-to-back matches after a five-game winning streak, and while their position at second is secure for now, the manner of defeats will concern coach Ashish Nehra heading into the playoffs.

## Saturday's double-header

The playoff picture could shift significantly on Saturday. Punjab Kings host Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the PCA Stadium in Mohali in an afternoon fixture, followed by Delhi Capitals against Rajasthan Royals at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. A PBKS win would take them to 15 points and all but guarantee qualification; a loss would leave them sweating on other results. For RCB, the match is about consolidating top spot and the crucial advantage of a Qualifier 1 berth.

## The NRI watch party

For diaspora cricket fans, the final two weeks of the league stage have become appointment viewing. IPL broadcast rights, available on JioStar across 120 countries, have made it easier than ever for NRIs to follow every ball. Fan groups in the US and UK report record attendance at pub screenings, and social media timelines are thick with memes about sleep deprivation — the time difference means most matches start at 5:30 AM or 10 AM on the American East Coast.

R. Ashwin, offering his analysis on his widely-followed YouTube channel, noted that this season's competitiveness reflected the IPL's maturing talent pool. "The gap between the top and bottom has never been smaller," he said, adding that Punjab Kings' struggles this week — a point picked up by several former cricketers — were less about individual failure and more about the relentless depth across squads.

## What's next

The league stage runs through May 24, with the Qualifier 1 in Dharamshala on May 26, the Eliminator in Chandigarh on May 27, and the final at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad on May 31. For at least four teams, every remaining match is now effectively a knockout.
